question: What is the primary goal of disease control in public health?

options.A: Eliminating the need for routine vaccination campaigns
options.B: Reducing disease incidence and mortality to acceptable levels
options.C: Isolating every infected patient in a national hospital
options.D: Completely removing all pathogens from the human body

explanation: Disease control focuses on lowering the burden of illness to manageable public health thresholds. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h1)

question: Why does public health practice prioritize interrupting transmission chains over individual treatment?

options.A: Individual hospital treatment is too expensive for government
options.B: Stopping spread protects the wider community from infection
options.C: Patients refuse to take medications prescribed by nurses
options.D: Pathogens cannot survive outside a single human host

explanation: Interrupted transmission prevents new cases from occurring in the population at large. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h1)

question: What term describes the constant presence of a disease in a specific geographic area?
explanation: An endemic disease maintains a predictable, steady baseline presence within a region. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h2)

question: A sudden surge of cholera cases in a state where it rarely occurs is best classified as what?
explanation: An unexpected rise above normal baseline levels in a specific area is an epidemic. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h2)

question: What defines the complete global reduction of a specific disease to zero cases?
explanation: Eradication means the pathogen no longer exists anywhere on earth naturally. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h3)

question: Why must a country maintain vaccination programs even after achieving regional elimination of a disease?

options.A: Eliminated diseases always return within exactly one year
options.B: Imported cases from other areas can restart transmission
options.C: Local pathogens mutate spontaneously inside healthy people
options.D: Global health organizations force countries to buy vaccines

explanation: Porous borders allow pathogens to cross back into regions that previously achieved elimination. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h3)

question: Which intervention is a classic example of primary disease prevention?
explanation: Immunization stops disease before it ever starts, which defines primary prevention. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h4)

question: A community nurse organizing blood pressure screening at a market square is practicing which level of prevention?
explanation: Screening detects existing hidden disease early so treatment can start before complications develop. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a public health surveillance system?

options.A: Collecting and analyzing health data to guide interventions
options.B: Punishing clinics that fail to report patient admissions
options.C: Conducting laboratory research on new pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: Providing free medications to chronically ill patients

explanation: Surveillance gathers data continuously to detect trends and direct public health actions. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h5)

question: A clinic nurse notices an unusual cluster of watery diarrhea and immediately reports it through official channels. What system is being utilized?
explanation: Reporting unusual clusters of symptoms is a core component of active disease surveillance. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h5)

question: What is the first logical step when health authorities suspect a disease outbreak?

options.B: Closing all schools and public markets
options.C: Ordering millions of vaccines from abroad
options.D: Confirming the existence of the outbreak

explanation: Investigators must first verify that reported cases exceed normal baseline expectancy before launching a full response. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h6)

question: During an outbreak investigation, why do epidemiologists analyze cases by time, place, and person?

options.A: To identify the source and mode of disease transmission
options.B: To write history books about past infectious diseases
options.C: To determine how much money the government should spend
options.D: To prove that nurses are working hard in rural clinics

explanation: Descriptive epidemiology maps out patterns that reveal where and how the pathogen is spreading. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h6)

question: Which activity is a direct nursing responsibility in community disease control?

options.A: Funding international public health research grants
options.B: Passing national laws on environmental sanitation
options.D: Manufacturing antibiotics in national pharmaceutical plants

explanation: Nurses directly deliver preventative services such as immunizations directly to community members. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h7)

question: Why do community nurses work closely with traditional or religious leaders during disease control campaigns?

options.A: To build local trust and encourage community participation
options.B: To diagnose complex viral infections without a laboratory
options.C: To receive financial donations for the local health clinic
options.D: To enforce strict police arrests for non-compliant citizens

explanation: Engaging respected community leaders helps overcome hesitation and improves public cooperation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h7)
